interest: Shows postwar rubber-price diplomacy between the U.S. and Allied colonial powers, and inspections of looted Japanese rubber stocks.
overview: This State Department file (894.6176, spanning August 1945 through December 1946) details United States and Allied policy regarding natural, synthetic, and reclaimed rubber following the surrender of Japan. The collection documents high-level U.S. inter-agency discussions on post-war Far Eastern rubber price policy, efforts to establish competitive parity between synthetic GR-S and plantation rubber, and inquiries from private American manufacturers such as B.F. Goodrich regarding reparations claims against Japanese firms. A major portion consists of series documents from the Combined Rubber Committee evaluating quarterly requirements and allocating scarce global rubber supplies across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, South Africa, Denmark, Norway, Spain, and UNRRA. Finally, the file chronicles the allocation to the United States of 10,000 metric tons of natural rubber stockpiled in Japan, detailing inter-agency coordination between the State Department and the RFC Office of Rubber Reserve, as well as joint Anglo-American-Dutch port inspections to examine bale markings and production dates in order to substantiate restitution claims for rubber looted by Japan from Southeast Asia.

subfiles.about: Discussion between State Department and Rubber Development Corporation officials regarding procurement authority, international pricing negotiations, and synthetic versus natural rubber competition in the Far East.
subfiles.from: J. N. DuBarry, Commodities Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: State and the Rubber Development Corporation agree to keep postwar rubber prices moderate, leading future price talks with Britain, the Netherlands, France, and Thailand, while opposing a private industry mission to Malaya and the Indies unless official.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Rubber Price Policy for the Far East

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a letter from The B.F. Goodrich Company concerning Japanese rubber machinery and reparations claims to the Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs.
subfiles.from: Ray Hicks, Office of the Publication Board, Department of Commerce
subfiles.summary: Hicks forwards B.F. Goodrich's inquiry on Japanese rubber assets to Martin's division, requesting a copy of State's eventual reply.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum Regarding B.F. Goodrich Company Inquiry
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Inquiry from The B.F. Goodrich Company concerning unpaid balances owed by Yokohama Rubber Company and the possibility of obtaining Japanese rubber machinery via reparations for relocation to China or New Zealand.
subfiles.from: Norm Keeling, Manager, Washington Office, International Division, The B.F. Goodrich Company
subfiles.summary: Keeling tells Harter Goodrich is owed large sums by Yokohama Rubber Company, suggesting Harter press Pauley's Reparations Committee to let Goodrich acquire Japanese tire machinery for new China or New Zealand operations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Norm Keeling to Dow Harter on Yokohama Rubber Company Balances and Japanese Rubber Machinery

subfiles.about: Statement of State Department policy regarding the absence of established machinery for private reparations claims against Japanese industrial assets.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Martin tells Keeling no mechanism yet exists for American reparations claims, but an Inter-Allied Reparations Commission will eventually invite firms to claim interest in Japanese assets.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Norm Keeling on Reparations Policy and Japanese Assets
subfiles.to: Norm Keeling, Manager, Washington Office, International Division, The B.F. Goodrich Company

subfiles.about: Combined Rubber Committee note on the allocation to the United States of exportable rubber discovered in Japan and British conditions regarding pricing and provenance.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-21 allocates exportable Japanese rubber to the U.S., with Britain conditioning agreement on matching Far Eastern market prices and investigating the rubber's original ownership.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-21: Note on Allocation to the United States of Rubber Available in Japan

subfiles.about: Approval of a supplemental first-quarter allocation of 2,000 long tons of Malayan natural rubber to Canada.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-22 approves a 2,000-ton supplemental rubber allocation to Canada, shifted from British Malayan stock, due to low Canadian reserves and long shipping times.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-22: Note on Supplemental First Quarter Allocation to Canada

subfiles.about: Review of Australia's second-quarter rubber requirements, stock data, and application for liquid latex from Ceylon.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-23 grants Australia 6,900 tons of rubber for its shift from synthetic to natural rubber by late 1946, plus 60,000 gallons of latex split with New Zealand given limited Ceylon supply.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-23: Note on Second Quarter Requirements of Australia

subfiles.about: Statement of New Zealand's second-quarter rubber requirements, industrial usage breakdown, and request for Ceylon liquid latex.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-24 sets New Zealand's second-quarter allocation at 660 tons of rubber for tires and rubber goods, plus a share of 6,000 gallons of Ceylon latex with Australia.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-24: Note on Second Quarter Requirements of New Zealand

subfiles.about: Assessment of South Africa's second-quarter rubber requirements and review of stock, consumption, and import statistics.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-25 reviews South Africa's 1,800-ton rubber request from Ceylon and India, noting it declined to seek more given overall supply limits.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-25: Note on Second Quarter Requirements of South Africa

subfiles.about: Detailed summary of Denmark's second-quarter requests for crude rubber, liquid latex for medical products, Butyl, and reclaimed rubber.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-26 covers Denmark's 900-ton crude and 200-ton reclaim rubber request, stressing urgent need for latex for medical supplies depleted under German occupation, plus a Butyl rubber trial allocation.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-26: Note on Second Quarter Requirements of Denmark

subfiles.about: Review of Norway's second-quarter rubber allocations, increased tire factory capacity, and requests for natural rubber, latex, and Butyl.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-27 grants Norway 510 tons of rubber reflecting a 1939 tire-plant expansion program, plus latex for medical goods and Butyl rubber for tube manufacturing.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-27: Note on Second Quarter Requirements of Norway

subfiles.about: Summary of Spain's annual rubber needs, syndicate procurement through Pirelli, and bilateral tire manufacturing agreements with Portugal.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-28 covers Spain's 6,000-ton annual rubber needs, a Pirelli-brokered 250-ton purchase attempt, and a Spain-Portugal arrangement to manufacture Portuguese-colony rubber into tires.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-28: Note on Second Quarter Requirements of Spain

subfiles.about: Presentation of an UNRRA request for 300 metric tons of natural liquid latex for medical rehabilitation in Byelorussia and Ukraine.
subfiles.from: Combined Rubber Committee
subfiles.summary: CRC-29 covers UNRRA's request for 300 tons of latex for Byelorussia and Ukraine's medical needs, though UK supply could meet only a fraction.
subfiles.title: Combined Rubber Committee Document CRC-29: Note on UNRRA Request for Second Quarter Allocation of Liquid Latex

subfiles.about: Confirmation of War Department intelligence indicating that 10,000 metric tons of natural rubber were available for export from Japan.
subfiles.from: William T. Phillips, Special Assistant to the Chief, International Resources Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Phillips confirms to Baird that 10,000 tons of natural rubber in Tokyo were available for export, per a War Department cable, supporting the U.S. allocation claim.
subfiles.title: Letter from William T. Phillips to Enid Baird Confirming Rubber Availability in Japan

subfiles.about: State Department request to the Office of Rubber Reserve to record identifying markings on Japanese rubber shipments to investigate possible looting.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Martin asks Baybutt to have Rubber Reserve inspect incoming Japanese rubber shipments and log identifying markings to help determine if the rubber was looted from Southeast Asia.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Richard Baybutt Requesting Inspection of Japanese Rubber Markings
subfiles.to: Richard Baybutt, Deputy Director, Office of Rubber Reserve, Reconstruction Finance Corporation

subfiles.about: Agreement by the Office of Rubber Reserve to instruct port agents to examine and record identifying marks on rubber arriving from Japan.
subfiles.from: Richard Baybutt, Deputy Director, Office of Rubber Reserve, Reconstruction Finance Corporation
subfiles.summary: Baybutt confirms Rubber Reserve will log markings on the 10,000-ton Japanese rubber allocation to check for looting, with shipments due at U.S. ports by June 1946.
subfiles.title: Letter from Richard Baybutt to Edwin M. Martin Agreeing to Inspect Japanese Rubber Markings
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: File record copy of the State Department's April 18, 1946 instructions to inspect incoming Japanese rubber for identifying markings.
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: File copy of Martin's letter to Baybutt confirming the 10,000-ton Japanese rubber allocation and requiring marking documentation to assess looting claims.
subfiles.title: File Copy of Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Richard Baybutt on Japanese Rubber Inspection
subfiles.to: Richard Baybutt, Deputy Director, Office of Rubber Reserve, Reconstruction Finance Corporation

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum discussing total Japanese rubber stockpiles, General MacArthur's export limitations, and Lend-Lease settlement restrictions.
subfiles.from: Harlan P. Bramble, International Resources Division, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Bramble reports a 24,248-ton Japanese rubber stockpile, of which MacArthur authorized exporting only 10,000 tons; Lend-Lease financing is unavailable due to the 1945 cutoff date with Britain.
subfiles.title: Internal Memorandum from Harlan P. Bramble to William T. Phillips on Japanese Rubber Stockpiles and Lend-Lease
subfiles.to: William T. Phillips, International Resources Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: State Department follow-up requesting a summary report on cargo markings and quantities of Japanese rubber received by the Office of Rubber Reserve.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Whitman asks Baybutt for a summary report on markings of Japanese rubber delivered to Rubber Reserve as of September 1946, to verify provenance for Allied inquiries.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Richard Baybutt Requesting Summary Markings Report
subfiles.to: Richard Baybutt, Deputy Director, Office of Rubber Reserve, Reconstruction Finance Corporation

subfiles.about: Request from the Department of Commerce for State Department review and political redaction of public reports on rubber conditions in liberated Asian territories.
subfiles.from: E. G. Holt, Rubber Advisor, Commodities Branch, Office of International Trade, Department of Commerce
subfiles.summary: Holt sends Kennedy draft reports on postwar rubber conditions in former Japanese-occupied territories, already screened by Commerce, asking State to clear any sensitive wording before release.
subfiles.title: Letter from E. G. Holt to Donald Kennedy on Liberated Areas Rubber Reports
subfiles.to: Donald Kennedy, Director, International Resources Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: British Embassy request to inspect Japanese rubber imports for production dates in addition to origin markings to substantiate restitution claims for looted colonial assets.
subfiles.from: C. B. Wilson, Raw Materials Section, British Embassy
subfiles.summary: Wilson reports joint British-Dutch-American inspections of two-thirds of Japan's 10,000-ton rubber allocation, with Britain planning FEC restitution claims for looted rubber; he asks U.S. inspectors to help date the remaining cargo.
subfiles.title: Letter from C. B. Wilson to I. M. Paige on Restitution Claims and Rubber Age Determination
subfiles.to: I. M. Paige, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of British Embassy representations regarding the feasibility of determining production dates of rubber imported from Japan.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Whitman tells Wilson the British production-dating request has been referred to Rubber Reserve to assess feasibility, promising to notify the Embassy once determined.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to C. B. Wilson Acknowledging British Restitution Request
subfiles.to: C. B. Wilson, Raw Materials Section, British Embassy

subfiles.about: State Department endorsement of the British request to determine production dates of imported Japanese rubber and follow-up on the overdue summary markings report.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Whitman forwards Wilson's letter, recommending Rubber Reserve comply with Britain's request to date Japanese rubber for FEC restitution claims, and asks about the pending cargo inspection report.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Richard Baybutt Endorsing British Inspection Request
subfiles.to: Richard Baybutt, Deputy Director, Office of Rubber Reserve, Reconstruction Finance Corporation
